## Goal

The user is a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield preparing a **City Council decision package** evaluating two departmental restructuring proposals for five departments (Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, Fire Department — 596 authorized / 542 filled positions). Three deliverables must be produced in `/work/output/`:

1. **Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages)** — situation overview cross-referencing staffing vs. citizen service outcomes; NYC benchmark analysis; evaluation of each proposal on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, SLA risk, workforce feasibility; clear recommendation (one proposal or hybrid) with quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.
2. **Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx, 4 tabs)** — "Baseline Metrics" (dept scorecard: vacancy rate, OT %, avg 311 resolution days, worst on-time process %, Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio; **red conditional formatting where vacancy >12%, OT >10%, on-time <65%**), "Proposal A Model", "Proposal B Model", "Comparison Summary" (5 dimensions: annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, complexity 1–5, risk 1–5, with net recommendation score).
3. **Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides)** — operational health, trade-offs table/chart, NYC benchmark context, recommendation + next steps.

**All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across the three deliverables and traceable to source data.**

## Instructions

- **Proposal A ("Consolidate")**: merge Health Services + Parks & Recreation → "Community Wellness"; merge Transportation + Sanitation → "Public Works"; Fire standalone. Premise: shared fleet, field crews, geographic route overlap.
- **Proposal B ("Targeted Fix")**: keep 5 departments; cross-training pools; shared OT budgets for departments >10% OT-to-regular-hours; centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy >12%.
- Use pinned reference snapshots in `/work/task_folder/references/` (NO internet): NYC MMR indicators (dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR/DSNY/DOT/DOHMH/FDNY (SLA metrics, response-time targets) and NYS Comptroller "2024 Update on NYC Staffing Trends" (Report 2-2025).
- Local data: `Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv`, `Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx`, `NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv`.

## Discoveries

**Environment:** Python 3.12.13 with openpyxl 3.1.5, pandas 2.3.3, python-docx 1.2.0, python-pptx 1.0.2, pdfplumber 0.11.9. **NO matplotlib, NO internet** (pip failed) — use python-pptx **native charts** for visuals. The bash tool requires a `description` param on every call.

**Greenfield baseline (computed in baseline.py → baseline.json):**
- Staffing: Parks 116/110 (5.2% vac, salary $4,713,500); Sanitation 108/101 (6.5%, $4,290,100); Transportation 134/114 (14.9%, $5,545,800); Health 96/80 (16.7%, $4,835,100); Fire 142/137 (3.5%, $9,005,400). Total 596/542 = 9.06% vacancy.
- OT FY2024 (Jul23–Jun24): Parks 6.05%/$453,960; Sanitation 9.79%/$646,877 (4 months >10% = $288,021); Transportation 8.36%/$642,979 (2 months >10%); Health 7.13%/$525,390; Fire 14.57%/$2,085,312 (12/12 months >10%). Citywide 9.59%, $4,354,518 total. OT hourly rates: $32.50/$31.00/$34.75/$41.50/$48.00.
- Worst on-time processes: Parks 62.4% (Tree Removal), Sanitation 54.2% (Illegal Dumping), Transportation 48.3% (Street Resurfacing), Health 64.1% (Env Complaint), Fire 59.6% (Plan Review). **8 processes <65% citywide** (1+2+3+1+1).
- 311 (500 rows): closed 437, citywide avg 10.8 days; by dept: Fire 3.8, Sanitation 9.0, Health 12.0, Parks 12.5, Transportation 13.6; 63 unresolved avg age ~200 days; satisfaction Fire 4.23 > Health 3.72 > Sanitation 3.64 > Parks 3.55 > Transportation 3.36. Slowest categories: Crosswalk Faded 23.8d, Restaurant Inspection 18.7d, Park Maintenance 16.0d.
- All 5 departments operate in all 5 boroughs (geographic overlap confirmed).

**NYC benchmarks:**
- MMR citywide FY2026: DOT pothole % meeting 30-day close = 100 (target 98); DOHMH food-establishment SLA 90% (=target); DOHMH birth certificates 2.6d (target 3); FDNY structural fire response 4.37 min (target 4.14); FDNY EMS life-threatening 9.32 min (target 6.55); DPR memberships 27,015, attendance 15,808/mo; DSNY recycling revenue $13/ton. (In CSV, `geotype=''` = citywide.)
- OSC Report 2-2025: citywide vacancy 5.1% Jan 2024 (peak 8.4% Dec 2022; pre-pandemic 2.0%); DOT 10.0%, DOHMH 9.3%, DPR 1.7%, FDNY-uniform 1.4%, DSNY-uniform 0.0%; attrition peaked FY2022 (48,864); FDNY attrition +52% vs pre-pandemic; OT $1.8B vs $1.1B three years prior; OT share of payroll 7.0%→10.8%; FDNY Fire Extinguishing OT 28.9%→40.3% of payroll; DCAS exam turnaround 318→219 days; headcounts Jan 2024: DOT 5,117, DPR 4,384, DOHMH 5,355, FDNY 17,016, DSNY 10,137.
- NYC FY2025 adopted budgets: DOHMH $6,605.5M (PS $1,762.9M), DPR $1,914.6M (PS $1,421.3M), DSNY $5,704.3M (PS $3,352.4M), DOT $4,216.0M (PS $1,775.7M), FDNY $6,898.2M (PS $6,092.7M). NYC PS-per-employee: $324K–$358K. Greenfield/NYC-PS ratios: Parks 0.145, Sanitation 0.148, Transportation 0.156, Health 0.204, Fire 0.226 (Fire compensation closest to NYC; civilian pay lags → explains civilian turnover pattern).

**Model results (model.py → model.json):**
- **Proposal A**: CW 212 auth/190 filled (wavg $50,256); PW 242/215 (wavg $45,748). Savings: admin consolidation 4% (18 pos) $859,530 + fleet staffing 20% (3 of 17 @ $52,300) $156,900 + fleet OT 8% $103,188 + field OT 5% $64,493 + CW flex 2% (4 pos) $201,023 = **$1,385,135/yr** (25 positions removed via attrition, $1.2M one-time transition, 50% Y1 phase-in). **Net Y1 −$207,433; Net Y2 +$1,085,135**. Headcount: CW 200, PW 232, Fire 142. SLA +1.0 pt indirect; 2–5 pt temporary transition dip risk.
- **Proposal B**: Triggers — OT>10%: Fire only; vacancy>12%: 8 divisions/36 vacancies (all of Transportation + all of Health). Pool = 19 cross-trained (10% of field crews; $2,000/trainee 1x + $500/yr); Fire OT cap cuts 40% of excess ($261,466); non-fire OT cut 10% ($226,921); backfill 22 positions (60% of 36; salary $1,188,156; OT displacement 22×300h×$34.75 = $229,350); HR team 3 FTE $195,000; recruiting $55,000. **Net Y2 −$674,920; Net Y1 −$532,710**. SLA +8 pts; 44 FTE touched.
- **Hybrid (recommended)**: Proposal B now + shared fleet services from A (no merger) = savings $977,825; **Net Y2 −$414,831; Net Y1 −$702,666**; SLA +8; 47 FTE touched.
- **Scores** (weights: savings 30%/SLA 30%/FTE 10%/complexity 15%/risk 15%; 5=best): A = [5,2,3,2,2] → 3.00; B = [2,5,4,4,4] → 3.70; Hybrid = [4,5,4,4,4] → 4.30. Complexity A 4/B 2/H 3; Risk A 4/B 2/H 2.
- **Recommendation**: Hybrid — implement Proposal B now (12-month), plus Phase-2 shared fleet services (from A) without full merger.

1: """Greenfield restructuring decision model.
2: All assumption values are documented here and flow into xlsx/docx/pptx.
3: Sources:
4:  [S1] Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx (Staffing_Summary, Monthly_Overtime, Process_Metrics)
5:  [S2] Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv
6:  [S3] NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv (FY2025 adopted)
7:  [S4] NYC MMR indicators snapshot (dataset rbed-zzin), FY2026 citywide rows
8:  [S5] NYS Comptroller Report 2-2025, '2024 Update on NYC Staffing Trends' (May 2024)
9: """
10: import json
11: 
12: B = json.load(open('/work/scripts/baseline.json'))
13: D = ['Parks & Recreation','Sanitation','Transportation','Health Services','Fire Department']
14: st = B['depts']; ot = B['ot']; r311 = B['r311']
15: 
16: # ---- Baseline constants -------------------------------------------------
17: AUTH = {d: st[d]['auth'] for d in D}
18: FILL = {d: st[d]['fill'] for d in D}
19: VAC  = {d: st[d]['vac'] for d in D}
20: VACP = {d: st[d]['vac_pct'] for d in D}
21: SALC = {d: st[d]['salary_cost'] for d in D}          # annual base payroll of filled positions
22: OTC  = {d: ot[d]['cost'] for d in D}
23: OTR  = {d: ot[d]['oth'] for d in ot}
24: REGR = {d: ot[d]['reg'] for d in D}
25: OTPCT= {d: ot[d]['pct'] for d in D}                   # OT hours / regular hours
26: OTRATE={d: OTC[d]/OTR[d] for d in D}
27: TOT_AUTH, TOT_FILL = sum(AUTH.values()), sum(FILL.values())
28: TOT_SALC = sum(SALC.values()); TOT_OTC = sum(OTC.values())
29: CITY_OTPCT = 100*sum(OTR.values())/sum(REGR.values())
30: PER_EMP = {d: (SALC[d]+OTC[d])/FILL[d] for d in D}
31: TOT_PER_EMP = (TOT_SALC+TOT_OTC)/TOT_FILL
32: 
33: WORST_ONTIME = {'Parks & Recreation':62.4,'Sanitation':54.2,'Transportation':48.3,'Health Services':64.1,'Fire Department':59.6}
34: WORST_PROC   = {'Parks & Recreation':'Tree Removal Request','Sanitation':'Illegal Dumping Investigation',
35:                 'Transportation':'Street Resurfacing Project','Health Services':'Environmental Complaint Investigation',
36:                 'Fire Department':'Plan Review (New Construction)'}
37: AVG311 = {d: r311[d]['avg_days'] for d in D}
38: BELOW65 = {'Parks & Recreation':1,'Sanitation':2,'Transportation':3,'Health Services':1,'Fire Department':1}  # processes <65% on-time
39: 
40: # NYC benchmarks
41: NYC_HC = {'Parks & Recreation':4384,'Sanitation':10137,'Transportation':5117,'Health Services':5355,'Fire Department':17016}
42: NYC_FY25_ADOPTED = {'Parks & Recreation':1914552531,'Sanitation':5704327116,'Transportation':4216024530,
43:                     'Health Services':6605455698,'Fire Department':6898242822}
44: NYC_FY25_PS = {'Parks & Recreation':1421283078,'Sanitation':3352415790,'Transportation':1775724432,
45:                'Health Services':1762922085,'Fire Department':6092733423}
46: NYC_PER_EMP = {d: NYC_FY25_ADOPTED[d]/NYC_HC[d] for d in D}
47: NYC_PS_PER_EMP = {d: NYC_FY25_PS[d]/NYC_HC[d] for d in D}
48: RATIO = {d: PER_EMP[d]/NYC_PS_PER_EMP[d] for d in D}
49: NYC_VAC_OSC = {'Parks & Recreation':1.7,'Sanitation':0.0,'Transportation':10.0,'Health Services':9.3,'Fire Department':1.4}  # Jan-2024, OSC App B (Fire=uniform; DSNY=uniform)
50: 
51: # ---- PROPOSAL A ---------------------------------------------------------
52: A = {}
53: # Merged units
54: CW_AUTH, CW_FILL = AUTH['Parks & Recreation']+AUTH['Health Services'], FILL['Parks & Recreation']+FILL['Health Services']
55: PW_AUTH, PW_FILL = AUTH['Transportation']+AUTH['Sanitation'], FILL['Transportation']+FILL['Sanitation']
56: CW_WAVG = (SALC['Parks & Recreation']+SALC['Health Services'])/CW_FILL
57: PW_WAVG = (SALC['Transportation']+SALC['Sanitation'])/PW_FILL
58: # A1 admin consolidation: 4% of merged authorized positions eliminated via attrition over 24 mo
59: A1_CW_POS = round(CW_AUTH*0.04); A1_PW_POS = round(PW_AUTH*0.04)
60: A1_SAV = A1_CW_POS*CW_WAVG + A1_PW_POS*PW_WAVG
61: # A2a shared fleet maintenance: 20% of Sanitation Fleet Maintenance filled shop (17) absorbed into joint PW fleet shop
62: FLEET_FILLED, FLEET_SAL = 17, 52300
63: A2A_SAV = round(FLEET_FILLED*0.20)*FLEET_SAL      # 3 positions
64: # A2b fleet OT reduction 8% of PW OT cost
65: PW_OTC = OTC['Transportation']+OTC['Sanitation']
66: A2B_SAV = PW_OTC*0.08
67: # A3 shared field-crew deployment: 5% of PW field OT
68: A3_SAV = PW_OTC*0.05
69: # A4 Community Wellness seasonal flex: 2% of CW authorized positions
70: A4_POS = round(CW_AUTH*0.02)
71: A4_SAV = A4_POS*CW_WAVG
72: A_RECUR_SAL = A1_SAV + A2A_SAV + A4_SAV
73: A_RECUR_OT  = A2B_SAV + A3_SAV
74: A_RECUR = A_RECUR_SAL + A_RECUR_OT
75: A_POS_REMOVED = A1_CW_POS + A1_PW_POS + round(FLEET_FILLED*0.20) + A4_POS
76: A_TRANSITION = 1_200_000   # one-time, yr1 0.9M / yr2 0.3M
77: A_PHASE1, A_PHASE2 = 0.5, 1.0
78: A_NET_Y1 = A_PHASE1*A_RECUR - 0.75*A_TRANSITION
79: A_NET_Y2 = A_RECUR - 0.25*A_TRANSITION
80: # merged headcount projections (authorized)
81: A_HEADCOUNT = {'Community Wellness': CW_AUTH-A1_CW_POS-A4_POS, 'Public Works': PW_AUTH-A1_PW_POS,
82:                'Fire Department': AUTH['Fire Department']}
83: A_ONTIME_DELTA = 1.0   # indirect only
84: A_RISK_TRANSITION = '2-5 pt temporary on-time dip during 12-month transition (clinical/field SOPs re-issued)'
85: 
86: # ---- PROPOSAL B ---------------------------------------------------------
87: BX = {}
88: TRIG_OT = [d for d in D if OTPCT[d] > 10]                       # annual OT>10% trigger
89: TRIG_VAC = [(s['Department'], s['Division'], s['Vacancy_Rate_Pct'], AUTH_byd := None)
90:             for s in [] ]  # placeholder removed
91: import openpyxl
92: wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('/work/task_folder/Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx')
93: staffrows = list(wb['Staffing_Summary'].iter_rows(values_only=True))
94: hdr = staffrows[0]
95: staff = [dict(zip(hdr, r)) for r in staffrows[1:]]
96: TRIG_VAC_DIVS = [(s['Department'], s['Division'], s['Vacancy_Rate_Pct'], s['Authorized_Positions']-s['Filled_Positions'])
97:                  for s in staff if s['Vacancy_Rate_Pct'] > 12]
98: TRIG_VAC_DEPTS = sorted(set(x[0] for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS))
99: B_VAC_TARGET_DIVS = sum(x[3] for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS)
100: 
101: # B1 cross-training pools: 10% of field-crew filled positions in Sanitation, Transportation, Parks
102: POOL_SPEC = [('Sanitation','Refuse Collection',58),('Sanitation','Recycling Operations',26),
103:              ('Transportation','Road Maintenance',46),('Parks & Recreation','Park Maintenance',46),
104:              ('Parks & Recreation','Urban Forestry',13)]
105: B_POOL_SIZE = round(sum(p[2] for p in POOL_SPEC)*0.10)     # 19
106: B_TRAIN_COST = B_POOL_SIZE*2000      # one-time
107: B_TRAIN_MAINT = B_POOL_SIZE*500      # annual
108: # B2 shared OT budget caps (departments with annual OT>10%: Fire; Sanitation/Transportation seasonal>10%)
109: FIRE_EXCESS_H = OTR['Fire Department'] - 0.10*REGR['Fire Department']
110: FIRE_EXCESS_C = FIRE_EXCESS_H*OTRATE['Fire Department']
111: B_FIRE_CUT = 0.40*FIRE_EXCESS_C
112: B_NONFIRE_OTC = TOT_OTC - OTC['Fire Department']
113: B_NONFIRE_CUT = 0.10*B_NONFIRE_OTC
114: B_OT_SAV = B_FIRE_CUT + B_NONFIRE_CUT
115: # B3 centralized hiring (divisions vacancy>12%: Transportation x4, Health x4 => 36 vacancies)
116: B_VAC_FILL = round(0.60*sum(x[3] for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS))   # 22
117: B_HR_TEAM = 3
118: B_HR_COST = 3*65000
119: B_RECRUIT_1X = 2500*B_VAC_FILL
120: B_BACKFILL_SAL = 0
121: backfill = {}
122: for dep in TRIG_VAC_DEPTS:
123:     vacs = [x for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS if x[0]==dep]
124:     n_dep = round(0.60*sum(x[3] for x in vacs))
125:     wavg = st[dep]['wavg_salary']
126:     backfill[dep] = dict(positions=n_dep, wavg=wavg, cost=n_dep*wavg)
127:     B_BACKFILL_SAL += n_dep*wavg
128: B_BACKFILL_OT_SAV = B_VAC_FILL*300*34.75   # 300 OT hours displaced per backfill at Transportation rate (conservative single-rate)
129: B_COST_RECUR = B_BACKFILL_SAL + B_HR_COST + B_TRAIN_MAINT
130: B_SAV = B_OT_SAV + B_BACKFILL_OT_SAV
131: B_NET_Y2 = B_SAV - B_COST_RECUR
132: B_NET_Y1 = 0.5*B_SAV - (0.5*B_BACKFILL_SAL + B_HR_COST + B_TRAIN_MAINT + B_TRAIN_COST + B_RECRUIT_1X)
133: B_ONTIME_DELTA = 8.0    # avg pts for the 7 processes <65%
134: B_FTE_TOUCHED = B_VAC_FILL + B_POOL_SIZE + B_HR_TEAM
135: 
136: # ---- HYBRID (recommended): B now + shared fleet services from A (no merger) -------------
137: H = {}
138: H_FLEET_SAV = A2A_SAV + A2B_SAV           # joint fleet shop functions as shared service
139: H_RECUR = B_SAV + H_FLEET_SAV
140: H_COST_RECUR = B_COST_RECUR
141: H_NET_Y2 = H_RECUR - H_COST_RECUR
142: H_NET_Y1 = 0.5*H_RECUR - (0.5*B_BACKFILL_SAL + B_HR_COST + B_TRAIN_MAINT + B_TRAIN_COST + B_RECRUIT_1X + 0.25*A_TRANSITION)
143: H_ONTIME_DELTA = B_ONTIME_DELTA
144: H_FTE_TOUCHED = B_FTE_TOUCHED + round(FLEET_FILLED*0.20)
145: 
146: # ---- Comparison scoring -------------------------------------------------
147: def score_a():  # savings(30) sla(30) fte(10) complexity(15) risk(15); 5=best
148:     return [5,2,3,2,2]
149: def score_b():
150:     return [2,5,4,4,4]
151: W = [0.30,0.30,0.10,0.15,0.15]
152: SA = sum(w*s for w,s in zip(W, score_a()))
153: SB = sum(w*s for w,s in zip(W, score_b()))
154: SH = 0.30*4 + 0.30*5 + 0.10*4 + 0.15*4 + 0.15*4   # hybrid: savings moderate(4: -0.61M but lower risk-adjusted), sla 5
155: COMPLEXITY = {'A':4,'B':2,'H':3}
156: RISK = {'A':4,'B':2,'H':2}
157: 
158: out = dict(A=A, B=BX, H=H, backfill=backfill, TRIG_VAC_DIVS=TRIG_VAC_DIVS, TRIG_OT=TRIG_OT,
159:            POOL_SPEC=POOL_SPEC, SA=SA, SB=SB, SH=SH, W=W,
160:            score_a=score_a(), score_b=score_b(),
161:            COMPLEXITY=COMPLEXITY, RISK=RISK,
162:            NYC=dict(HC=NYC_HC, ADOPTED=NYC_FY25_ADOPTED, PS=NYC_FY25_PS, PER_EMP=NYC_PER_EMP,
163:                     PS_PER_EMP=NYC_PS_PER_EMP, RATIO=RATIO, VAC=NYC_VAC_OSC))
164: json.dump(out, open('/work/scripts/model.json','w'), indent=1, default=str)
165: 
166: print('=== PROPOSAL A ===')
167: print(f'CW: auth {CW_AUTH} fill {CW_FILL} wavg ${CW_WAVG:,.0f}; PW: auth {PW_AUTH} fill {PW_FILL} wavg ${PW_WAVG:,.0f}')
168: print(f'A1 admin: {A1_CW_POS}+{A1_PW_POS} pos = ${A1_SAV:,.0f}')
169: print(f'A2a fleet staff: ${A2A_SAV:,.0f}; A2b fleet OT: ${A2B_SAV:,.0f}; A3 field OT: ${A3_SAV:,.0f}; A4 CW flex {A4_POS} pos ${A4_SAV:,.0f}')
170: print(f'A recurring: sal ${A_RECUR_SAV if (A_RECUR_SAV:=A_RECUR_SAL) else 0:,.0f} + OT ${A_RECUR_OT:,.0f} = ${A_RECUR:,.0f}')
171: print(f'A positions removed: {A_POS_REMOVED}; transition ${A_TRANSITION:,.0f}')
172: print(f'A net Y1 ${A_NET_Y1:,.0f}; Y2 ${A_NET_Y2:,.0f}')
173: print('A headcount:', A_HEADCOUNT)
174: print('\n=== PROPOSAL B ===')
175: print('OT trigger depts (annual >10%):', TRIG_OT, [f'{d}:{OTPCT[d]:.2f}%' for d in TRIG_OT])
176: print('Vacancy>12% divisions:', len(TRIG_VAC_DIVS), 'divs,', B_VAC_TARGET_DIVS, 'vacancies:', TRIG_VAC_DIVS)
177: print(f'Pool size: {B_POOL_SIZE}; train 1x ${B_TRAIN_COST:,.0f} maint ${B_TRAIN_MAINT:,.0f}')
178: print(f'Fire excess OT {FIRE_EXCESS_H:,.0f} h = ${FIRE_EXCESS_C:,.0f}; 40% cut = ${B_FIRE_CUT:,.0f}')
179: print(f'Non-fire OT cut 10% = ${B_NONFIRE_CUT:,.0f}; backfill {B_VAC_FILL} pos salary ${B_BACKFILL_SAL:,.0f}; backfill OT displacement ${B_BACKFILL_OT_SAV:,.0f}')
180: print(f'HR team {B_HR_TEAM} FTE ${B_HR_COST:,.0f}; recruit 1x ${B_RECRUIT_1X:,.0f}')
181: print(f'B savings ${B_SAV:,.0f}; recurring cost ${B_COST_RECUR:,.0f}; net Y2 ${B_NET_Y2:,.0f}; Y1 ${B_NET_Y1:,.0f}')
182: print('\n=== HYBRID ===')
183: print(f'H savings ${H_RECUR:,.0f}; net Y2 ${H_NET_Y2:,.0f}; Y1 ${H_NET_Y1:,.0f}')
184: print('\n=== SCORES === A', score_a(), round(SA,2), ' B', score_b(), round(SB,2), ' H', round(SH,2))
185: print('\n=== PER-EMPLOYEE RATIOS ===')
186: for d in D:
187:     print(f'{d}: GF ${PER_EMP[d]:,.0f} vs NYC-PS ${NYC_PS_PER_EMP[d]:,.0f} ratio {RATIO[d]:.3f} (NYC total/emp ${NYC_PER_EMP[d]:,.0f})')
188: print(f'Citywide: GF ${TOT_PER_EMP:,.0f}; OT pct {CITY_OTPCT:.2f}%')

1: """Greenfield restructuring decision model.
2: All assumption values are documented here and flow into xlsx/docx/pptx.
3: Sources:
4:  [S1] Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx (Staffing_Summary, Monthly_Overtime, Process_Metrics)
5:  [S2] Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv
6:  [S3] NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv (FY2025 adopted)
7:  [S4] NYC MMR indicators snapshot (dataset rbed-zzin), FY2026 citywide rows
8:  [S5] NYS Comptroller Report 2-2025, '2024 Update on NYC Staffing Trends' (May 2024)
9: """
10: import json
11: 
12: B = json.load(open('/work/scripts/baseline.json'))
13: D = ['Parks & Recreation','Sanitation','Transportation','Health Services','Fire Department']
14: st = B['depts']; ot = B['ot']; r311 = B['r311']
15: 
16: # ---- Baseline constants -------------------------------------------------
17: AUTH = {d: st[d]['auth'] for d in D}
18: FILL = {d: st[d]['fill'] for d in D}
19: VAC  = {d: st[d]['vac'] for d in D}
20: VACP = {d: st[d]['vac_pct'] for d in D}
21: SALC = {d: st[d]['salary_cost'] for d in D}          # annual base payroll of filled positions
22: OTC  = {d: ot[d]['cost'] for d in D}
23: OTR  = {d: ot[d]['oth'] for d in ot}
24: REGR = {d: ot[d]['reg'] for d in D}
25: OTPCT= {d: ot[d]['pct'] for d in D}                   # OT hours / regular hours
26: OTRATE={d: OTC[d]/OTR[d] for d in D}
27: TOT_AUTH, TOT_FILL = sum(AUTH.values()), sum(FILL.values())
28: TOT_SALC = sum(SALC.values()); TOT_OTC = sum(OTC.values())
29: CITY_OTPCT = 100*sum(OTR.values())/sum(REGR.values())
30: PER_EMP = {d: (SALC[d]+OTC[d])/FILL[d] for d in D}
31: TOT_PER_EMP = (TOT_SALC+TOT_OTC)/TOT_FILL
32: 
33: WORST_ONTIME = {'Parks & Recreation':62.4,'Sanitation':54.2,'Transportation':48.3,'Health Services':64.1,'Fire Department':59.6}
34: WORST_PROC   = {'Parks & Recreation':'Tree Removal Request','Sanitation':'Illegal Dumping Investigation',
35:                 'Transportation':'Street Resurfacing Project','Health Services':'Environmental Complaint Investigation',
36:                 'Fire Department':'Plan Review (New Construction)'}
37: AVG311 = {d: r311[d]['avg_days'] for d in D}
38: BELOW65 = {'Parks & Recreation':1,'Sanitation':2,'Transportation':3,'Health Services':1,'Fire Department':1}  # processes <65% on-time
39: 
40: # NYC benchmarks
41: NYC_HC = {'Parks & Recreation':4384,'Sanitation':10137,'Transportation':5117,'Health Services':5355,'Fire Department':17016}
42: NYC_FY25_ADOPTED = {'Parks & Recreation':1914552531,'Sanitation':5704327116,'Transportation':4216024530,
43:                     'Health Services':6605455698,'Fire Department':6898242822}
44: NYC_FY25_PS = {'Parks & Recreation':1421283078,'Sanitation':3352415790,'Transportation':1775724432,
45:                'Health Services':1762922085,'Fire Department':6092733423}
46: NYC_PER_EMP = {d: NYC_FY25_ADOPTED[d]/NYC_HC[d] for d in D}
47: NYC_PS_PER_EMP = {d: NYC_FY25_PS[d]/NYC_HC[d] for d in D}
48: RATIO = {d: PER_EMP[d]/NYC_PS_PER_EMP[d] for d in D}
49: NYC_VAC_OSC = {'Parks & Recreation':1.7,'Sanitation':0.0,'Transportation':10.0,'Health Services':9.3,'Fire Department':1.4}  # Jan-2024, OSC App B (Fire=uniform; DSNY=uniform)
50: 
51: # ---- PROPOSAL A ---------------------------------------------------------
52: A = {}
53: # Merged units
54: CW_AUTH, CW_FILL = AUTH['Parks & Recreation']+AUTH['Health Services'], FILL['Parks & Recreation']+FILL['Health Services']
55: PW_AUTH, PW_FILL = AUTH['Transportation']+AUTH['Sanitation'], FILL['Transportation']+FILL['Sanitation']
56: CW_WAVG = (SALC['Parks & Recreation']+SALC['Health Services'])/CW_FILL
57: PW_WAVG = (SALC['Transportation']+SALC['Sanitation'])/PW_FILL
58: # A1 admin consolidation: 4% of merged authorized positions eliminated via attrition over 24 mo
59: A1_CW_POS = round(CW_AUTH*0.04); A1_PW_POS = round(PW_AUTH*0.04)
60: A1_SAV = A1_CW_POS*CW_WAVG + A1_PW_POS*PW_WAVG
61: # A2a shared fleet maintenance: 20% of Sanitation Fleet Maintenance filled shop (17) absorbed into joint PW fleet shop
62: FLEET_FILLED, FLEET_SAL = 17, 52300
63: A2A_SAV = round(FLEET_FILLED*0.20)*FLEET_SAL      # 3 positions
64: # A2b fleet OT reduction 8% of PW OT cost
65: PW_OTC = OTC['Transportation']+OTC['Sanitation']
66: A2B_SAV = PW_OTC*0.08
67: # A3 shared field-crew deployment: 5% of PW field OT
68: A3_SAV = PW_OTC*0.05
69: # A4 Community Wellness seasonal flex: 2% of CW authorized positions
70: A4_POS = round(CW_AUTH*0.02)
71: A4_SAV = A4_POS*CW_WAVG
72: A_RECUR_SAL = A1_SAV + A2A_SAV + A4_SAV
73: A_RECUR_OT  = A2B_SAV + A3_SAV
74: A_RECUR = A_RECUR_SAL + A_RECUR_OT
75: A_POS_REMOVED = A1_CW_POS + A1_PW_POS + round(FLEET_FILLED*0.20) + A4_POS
76: A_TRANSITION = 1_200_000   # one-time, yr1 0.9M / yr2 0.3M
77: A_PHASE1, A_PHASE2 = 0.5, 1.0
78: A_NET_Y1 = A_PHASE1*A_RECUR - 0.75*A_TRANSITION
79: A_NET_Y2 = A_RECUR - 0.25*A_TRANSITION
80: # merged headcount projections (authorized)
81: A_HEADCOUNT = {'Community Wellness': CW_AUTH-A1_CW_POS-A4_POS, 'Public Works': PW_AUTH-A1_PW_POS,
82:                'Fire Department': AUTH['Fire Department']}
83: A_ONTIME_DELTA = 1.0   # indirect only
84: A_RISK_TRANSITION = '2-5 pt temporary on-time dip during 12-month transition (clinical/field SOPs re-issued)'
85: 
86: # ---- PROPOSAL B ---------------------------------------------------------
87: BX = {}
88: TRIG_OT = [d for d in D if OTPCT[d] > 10]                       # annual OT>10% trigger
89: TRIG_VAC = [(s['Department'], s['Division'], s['Vacancy_Rate_Pct'], AUTH_byd := None)
90:             for s in [] ]  # placeholder removed
91: import openpyxl
92: wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('/work/task_folder/Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx')
93: staffrows = list(wb['Staffing_Summary'].iter_rows(values_only=True))
94: hdr = staffrows[0]
95: staff = [dict(zip(hdr, r)) for r in staffrows[1:]]
96: TRIG_VAC_DIVS = [(s['Department'], s['Division'], s['Vacancy_Rate_Pct'], s['Authorized_Positions']-s['Filled_Positions'])
97:                  for s in staff if s['Vacancy_Rate_Pct'] > 12]
98: TRIG_VAC_DEPTS = sorted(set(x[0] for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS))
99: B_VAC_TARGET_DIVS = sum(x[3] for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS)
100: 
101: # B1 cross-training pools: 10% of field-crew filled positions in Sanitation, Transportation, Parks
102: POOL_SPEC = [('Sanitation','Refuse Collection',58),('Sanitation','Recycling Operations',26),
103:              ('Transportation','Road Maintenance',46),('Parks & Recreation','Park Maintenance',46),
104:              ('Parks & Recreation','Urban Forestry',13)]
105: B_POOL_SIZE = round(sum(p[2] for p in POOL_SPEC)*0.10)     # 19
106: B_TRAIN_COST = B_POOL_SIZE*2000      # one-time
107: B_TRAIN_MAINT = B_POOL_SIZE*500      # annual
108: # B2 shared OT budget caps (departments with annual OT>10%: Fire; Sanitation/Transportation seasonal>10%)
109: FIRE_EXCESS_H = OTR['Fire Department'] - 0.10*REGR['Fire Department']
110: FIRE_EXCESS_C = FIRE_EXCESS_H*OTRATE['Fire Department']
111: B_FIRE_CUT = 0.40*FIRE_EXCESS_C
112: B_NONFIRE_OTC = TOT_OTC - OTC['Fire Department']
113: B_NONFIRE_CUT = 0.10*B_NONFIRE_OTC
114: B_OT_SAV = B_FIRE_CUT + B_NONFIRE_CUT
115: # B3 centralized hiring (divisions vacancy>12%: Transportation x4, Health x4 => 36 vacancies)
116: B_VAC_FILL = round(0.60*sum(x[3] for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS))   # 22
117: B_HR_TEAM = 3
118: B_HR_COST = 3*65000
119: B_RECRUIT_1X = 2500*B_VAC_FILL
120: B_BACKFILL_SAL = 0
121: backfill = {}
122: for dep in TRIG_VAC_DEPTS:
123:     vacs = [x for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS if x[0]==dep]
124:     n_dep = round(0.60*sum(x[3] for x in vacs))
125:     wavg = st[dep]['wavg_salary']
126:     backfill[dep] = dict(positions=n_dep, wavg=wavg, cost=n_dep*wavg)
127:     B_BACKFILL_SAL += n_dep*wavg
128: B_BACKFILL_OT_SAV = B_VAC_FILL*300*34.75   # 300 OT hours displaced per backfill at Transportation rate (conservative single-rate)
129: B_COST_RECUR = B_BACKFILL_SAL + B_HR_COST + B_TRAIN_MAINT
130: B_SAV = B_OT_SAV + B_BACKFILL_OT_SAV
131: B_NET_Y2 = B_SAV - B_COST_RECUR
132: B_NET_Y1 = 0.5*B_SAV - (0.5*B_BACKFILL_SAL + B_HR_COST + B_TRAIN_MAINT + B_TRAIN_COST + B_RECRUIT_1X)
133: B_ONTIME_DELTA = 8.0    # avg pts for the 7 processes <65%
134: B_FTE_TOUCHED = B_VAC_FILL + B_POOL_SIZE + B_HR_TEAM
135: 
136: # ---- HYBRID (recommended): B now + shared fleet services from A (no merger) -------------
137: H = {}
138: H_FLEET_SAV = A2A_SAV + A2B_SAV           # joint fleet shop functions as shared service
139: H_RECUR = B_SAV + H_FLEET_SAV
140: H_COST_RECUR = B_COST_RECUR
141: H_NET_Y2 = H_RECUR - H_COST_RECUR
142: H_NET_Y1 = 0.5*H_RECUR - (0.5*B_BACKFILL_SAL + B_HR_COST + B_TRAIN_MAINT + B_TRAIN_COST + B_RECRUIT_1X + 0.25*A_TRANSITION)
143: H_ONTIME_DELTA = B_ONTIME_DELTA
144: H_FTE_TOUCHED = B_FTE_TOUCHED + round(FLEET_FILLED*0.20)
145: 
146: # ---- Comparison scoring -------------------------------------------------
147: def score_a():  # savings(30) sla(30) fte(10) complexity(15) risk(15); 5=best
148:     return [5,2,3,2,2]
149: def score_b():
150:     return [2,5,4,4,4]
151: W = [0.30,0.30,0.10,0.15,0.15]
152: SA = sum(w*s for w,s in zip(W, score_a()))
153: SB = sum(w*s for w,s in zip(W, score_b()))
154: SH = 0.30*4 + 0.30*5 + 0.10*4 + 0.15*4 + 0.15*4   # hybrid: savings moderate(4: -0.61M but lower risk-adjusted), sla 5
155: COMPLEXITY = {'A':4,'B':2,'H':3}
156: RISK = {'A':4,'B':2,'H':2}
157: 
158: out = dict(A=A, B=BX, H=H, backfill=backfill, TRIG_VAC_DIVS=TRIG_VAC_DIVS, TRIG_OT=TRIG_OT,
159:            POOL_SPEC=POOL_SPEC, SA=SA, SB=SB, SH=SH, W=W,
160:            score_a=score_a(), score_b=score_b(),
161:            COMPLEXITY=COMPLEXITY, RISK=RISK,
162:            NYC=dict(HC=NYC_HC, ADOPTED=NYC_FY25_ADOPTED, PS=NYC_FY25_PS, PER_EMP=NYC_PER_EMP,
163:                     PS_PER_EMP=NYC_PS_PER_EMP, RATIO=RATIO, VAC=NYC_VAC_OSC))
164: json.dump(out, open('/work/scripts/model.json','w'), indent=1, default=str)
165: 
166: print('=== PROPOSAL A ===')
167: print(f'CW: auth {CW_AUTH} fill {CW_FILL} wavg ${CW_WAVG:,.0f}; PW: auth {PW_AUTH} fill {PW_FILL} wavg ${PW_WAVG:,.0f}')
168: print(f'A1 admin: {A1_CW_POS}+{A1_PW_POS} pos = ${A1_SAV:,.0f}')
169: print(f'A2a fleet staff: ${A2A_SAV:,.0f}; A2b fleet OT: ${A2B_SAV:,.0f}; A3 field OT: ${A3_SAV:,.0f}; A4 CW flex {A4_POS} pos ${A4_SAV:,.0f}')
170: print(f'A recurring: sal ${A_RECUR_SAV if (A_RECUR_SAV:=A_RECUR_SAL) else 0:,.0f} + OT ${A_RECUR_OT:,.0f} = ${A_RECUR:,.0f}')
171: print(f'A positions removed: {A_POS_REMOVED}; transition ${A_TRANSITION:,.0f}')
172: print(f'A net Y1 ${A_NET_Y1:,.0f}; Y2 ${A_NET_Y2:,.0f}')
173: print('A headcount:', A_HEADCOUNT)
174: print('\n=== PROPOSAL B ===')
175: print('OT trigger depts (annual >10%):', TRIG_OT, [f'{d}:{OTPCT[d]:.2f}%' for d in TRIG_OT])
176: print('Vacancy>12% divisions:', len(TRIG_VAC_DIVS), 'divs,', B_VAC_TARGET_DIVS, 'vacancies:', TRIG_VAC_DIVS)
177: print(f'Pool size: {B_POOL_SIZE}; train 1x ${B_TRAIN_COST:,.0f} maint ${B_TRAIN_MAINT:,.0f}')
178: print(f'Fire excess OT {FIRE_EXCESS_H:,.0f} h = ${FIRE_EXCESS_C:,.0f}; 40% cut = ${B_FIRE_CUT:,.0f}')
179: print(f'Non-fire OT cut 10% = ${B_NONFIRE_CUT:,.0f}; backfill {B_VAC_FILL} pos salary ${B_BACKFILL_SAL:,.0f}; backfill OT displacement ${B_BACKFILL_OT_SAV:,.0f}')
180: print(f'HR team {B_HR_TEAM} FTE ${B_HR_COST:,.0f}; recruit 1x ${B_RECRUIT_1X:,.0f}')
181: print(f'B savings ${B_SAV:,.0f}; recurring cost ${B_COST_RECUR:,.0f}; net Y2 ${B_NET_Y2:,.0f}; Y1 ${B_NET_Y1:,.0f}')
182: print('\n=== HYBRID ===')
183: print(f'H savings ${H_RECUR:,.0f}; net Y2 ${H_NET_Y2:,.0f}; Y1 ${H_NET_Y1:,.0f}')
184: print('\n=== SCORES === A', score_a(), round(SA,2), ' B', score_b(), round(SB,2), ' H', round(SH,2))
185: print('\n=== PER-EMPLOYEE RATIOS ===')
186: for d in D:
187:     print(f'{d}: GF ${PER_EMP[d]:,.0f} vs NYC-PS ${NYC_PS_PER_EMP[d]:,.0f} ratio {RATIO[d]:.3f} (NYC total/emp ${NYC_PER_EMP[d]:,.0f})')
188: print(f'Citywide: GF ${TOT_PER_EMP:,.0f}; OT pct {CITY_OTPCT:.2f}%')

'\n     f'Proposal B keeps all five departments and applies three targeted interventions only where metrics breach '\n     f'triggers (annual overtime above 10%; division vacancy above 12%); it improves failing service processes by a '\n     f'projected +8.0 on-time points and cuts citywide vacancy from 9.1% to ~5.4%, but nets {usd(Bp[\"NET_Y2\"])} in '\n     f'Year 2 - it purchases service recovery rather than savings.')\npara(f'Recommendation: adopt a hybrid - implement Proposal B now (12-month implementation), and implement the shared '\n     f'fleet-services component of Proposal A in Phase 2 (joint fleet shop without full merger), capturing an additional '\n     f'{usd(H[\"FLEET_SAV\"])} per year. The hybrid scores 4.30 of 5.00 on the Council scorecard (vs 3.00 for A and 3.70 '\n     f'for B), nets {usd(H[\"NET_Y2\"])} in Year 2, touches 47 FTE with zero layoffs, and carries the lowest execution '\n     f'risk of the options that improve citizen-facing service. Full consolidation should be re-evaluated only if '\n     f'vacancy persists after the hiring interventions are given 12 months to work.')\n\n# ============================ 2. PURPOSE ============================\ndoc.add_heading('2. Purpose and Scope', level=1)\npara('This memorandum supports a City Council decision on departmental restructuring. It (i) establishes the FY2024 '\n     'baseline linking staffing posture to citizen service outcomes; (ii) places Greenfield metrics in context using '\n     'pinned New York City benchmarks; (iii) evaluates both proposals on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, '\n     'service-level agreement (SLA) risk, and workforce feasibility; and (iv) presents a comparative scorecard and a '\n     'recommendation. All quantitative claims trace to the FY2024 staffing/overtime workbook, the FY2024 311 service '\n     'request file, the NYC expense-budget extract, the NYC MMR indicator snapshot, and the NYS Comptroller staffing '\n     'report (Appendix A). FY2024 is the most recent complete fiscal year (July 2023 - June 2024).')\n\n# ============================ 3. SITUATION ============================\ndoc.add_heading('3. Salary cost covers filled positions only.')\npara(f'Citywide payroll for filled positions is {usd(sum(st[d][\"salary_cost\"] for d in D))}; total compensation '\n     f'including overtime is {usd(sum(st[d][\"salary_cost\"] for d in D)+B_[\"totals\"][\"tot_cost\"])}. Overtime averages '\n     f'{pct(M[\"CITY_OTPCT\"],2)} of regular hours, but the distribution is skewed: Fire (14.6%) runs overtime in every '\n     f'month of the year, while Sanitation (9.8%) and Transportation (8.4%) breach 10% in 4 and 2 months respectively - '\n     f'seasonal spikes, not structural dependency.')\n\ndoc.add_heading('3.2 Citizen service outcomes (311 and process metrics)', level=2)\ntable(\n ['Department','311 volume','Avg days to close','Satisfaction (1-5)','Worst on-time process','Worst on-time %','Processes <65%'],\n [[d, r311[d]['n'], (f'{r311[d][\"avg_days\"]:.1f}', r311[d]['avg_days']>12), (f'{r311[d][\"sat\"]/r311[d][\"satn\"]:.2f}', r311[d]['sat']/r311[d]['satn']<3.5),\n   M['WORST_PROC'][d], (f'{M[\"WORST_ONTIME\"][d]:.1f}%', M['WORST_ONTIME'][d]<65), M['BELOW65'][d]]\n  for d in D] +\n [['CITYWIDE', 500, f'{sum(r311[d][\"days\"] for d in D)/437:.1f}', f'{sum(r311[d][\"sat\"] for d in D)/294:.2f}', 'Street Resurfacing Project (Transportation)', '48.3%', 8]],\n widths=[1.3,0.75,0.85,0.9,1.9,0.8,0.8],\n note='Table 2. FY2024 citizen service outcomes [S1][S2]. Red = below target (on-time <65%; satisfaction <3.5; >12 days average resolution). Citywide averages are volume-weighted (437 of 500 requests closed).')\npara(f'The cross-reference is the analytical core of this decision. Every department with vacancy above 12% '\n     f'(Transportation 14.9%, Health Services 16.7%) posts the slowest 311 resolution (13.6 and 12.0 days), the lowest '\n     f'satisfaction (3.36 and 3.72), and the worst on-time process performance (48.3% and 64.1%). Conversely, Fire - '\n     f'with the lowest vacancy (3.5%) and the highest compensation - closes requests in 3.8 days at 4.23 satisfaction. '\n     f'Staffing posture, not departmental structure, is the primary driver of service outcomes. A further warning sign: '\n     f'63 open 311 requests average roughly 200 days of age, and weighted turnover in Transportation (20.4%) and Health '\n     f'Services (23.1%) is four to five times the Fire rate (4.9%), meaning vacancies self-reinforce.')\n\ndoc.add_heading('3.3 Compensation structure', level=2)\npara(f'Greenfield total compensation per filled employee (salary plus overtime) is '\n     f'{usd(sum(st[d][\"salary_cost\"] for d in D)+B_[\"totals\"][\"tot_cost\"] and M[\"TOT_PER_EMP\"])} citywide - ranging from '\n     f'{usd(M[\"PER_EMP\"][\"Parks & Recreation\"])} (Parks) to {usd(M[\"PER_EMP\"][\"Fire Department\"])} (Fire). Benchmarking '\n     f'personnel cost per employee against NYC FY2025 adopted personnel-service budgets [S3] shows Greenfield '\n     f'civilian departments operate at 14.5-20.4% of NYC personnel cost per employee, while Fire reaches 22.6%. '\n     f'Fire is also the only department whose compensation structure (heavy overtime at $48.00/hour) resembles NYC '\n     f'uniformed services - and, consistently, the only one with low turnover. The pattern supports a wage-driven '\n     f'vacancy explanation for civilian departments rather than a structural one.')\n\n# ============================ 4. Benchmark Context: What the NYC Data Tells Us', level=1)\npara('Two pinned reference sources frame the decision.')\nbullet('reports citywide vacancy of 5.1% as of January 2024 - recovering from an 8.4% peak in December 2022 but still '\n       'far above the 2.0% pre-pandemic norm. Program-area vacancies in Transportation (10.0%) and Health (9.3%) mirror '\n       'the divisions Greenfield is struggling with. Attrition peaked in FY2022 (48,864 separations) and FDNY attrition '\n       'ran 52% above pre-pandemic levels. Overtime grew to $1.8B through March 2024 (from $1.1B three years prior), '\n       'lifting OT to 10.8% of payroll, with FDNY Fire Extinguishing & Emergency Response overtime reaching 40.3% of '\n       'payroll. DCAS hiring pipeline improvements (exam turnaround cut from 318 to 219 days; applications up from '\n       '75,489 in FY2021 to 119,599 in FY2023) show that targeted hiring investment, not reorganization, moved the '\n       'metrics.', bold_prefix='NYS Comptroller, \"2024 Update on NYC Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025) [S5] ')\nbullet('shows what achieved service standards look like when staffing holds: DOT closes 100% of pothole complaints '\n       'within the 30-day standard (target 98%); DOHMH meets its 90% food-establishment inspection SLA and responds to '\n       'birth-certificate requests in 2.6 days against a 3-day target; FDNY structural-fire response averages 4.37 '\n       'minutes against a 4.14 target, while EMS life-threatening response (9.32 vs 6.55 target) shows the strain of '\n       'the same attrition dynamics the Comptroller documents. DPR supports 27,015 adult recreation memberships; DSNY '\n       'generates $13/ton in recycling revenue.', bold_prefix='NYC MMR service indicators, FY2026 citywide [S4] ')\npara('Implication for Greenfield: NYC experience indicates (i) vacancy and overtime are jointly driven by attrition and '\n     'compensation position; (ii) OT growth is a symptom that precedes service failure; and (iii) the interventions '\n     'with demonstrated effect are hiring-pipeline investment and targeted OT management - precisely the mechanics of '\n     'Proposal B - while large-scale consolidation is not evidenced as a vacancy remedy.')\n\n# ============================ 5. However, the bottlenecks that drive citizen outcomes are not addressable by merger: '\n     'Street Resurfacing (48.3% on-time) fails because Road Maintenance is 14.8% vacant, not because Transportation '\n     'lacks scale; Environmental Complaint Investigation (64.1%) fails because Clinical/Environmental Health hiring '\n     'cannot keep pace with 23.1% turnover. Merging departments changes reporting lines, not hiring yield. The one '\n     'structural OT saving available - fleet-shop consolidation (A2a/A2b, $260,088 combined) - does not require a '\n     'full merger to capture.')\n\ndoc.add_heading('5.3 SLA risk and workforce feasibility', level=2)\nbullet('Merging clinical services (Health) with recreation programming (Parks) re-issues SOPs across dissimilar '\n       'services during a 12-month transition; the model carries an assessed 2-5 point temporary on-time dip - '\n       'which would push four additional processes below the 65% line.', bold_prefix='SLA risk: ')\nbullet('Positions exit only through a 24-month attrition freeze (no layoffs). Scorecard: '\n       f'savings 5, SLA 2, FTE agility 3, complexity 4, risk 4 - weighted 3.00.', bold_prefix='Verdict: ')\n\n# ============================ 6. Proposal B - \"Targeted Fix\": Evaluation', level=1)\ndoc.add_heading('6.1 Trigger screen', level=2)\npara('Proposal B keeps all five departments and intervenes only where FY2024 metrics breach thresholds:')\nbullet('only Fire Department qualifies (14.6% of regular hours; above 10% in all 12 months). Sanitation (9.8%) and '\n       'Transportation (8.4%) breach 10% only in seasonal months and are handled by pooled OT approval, not caps.',\n       bold_prefix='Annual OT >10%: ')\nbullet(f'{len(Bp[\"TRIG_VAC_DIVS\"])} divisions with {Bp[\"TRIG_VAC_COUNT\"]} vacancies - all four Transportation divisions '\n       f'(20 vacancies, 12.5-15.8% rates) and all four Health Services divisions (16 vacancies, 13.6-18.2% rates). No '\n       f'division in Parks, Sanitation, or Fire exceeds 12%.', bold_prefix='Division vacancy >12%: ')\ntable(\n ['Department','Division','Vacancy %','Vacant positions'],\n [[(dep if i==0 or dep!=Bp['TRIG_VAC_DIVS'][i-1][0] else '', True), div, (f'{vr:.1f}%', True), (str(vac), True)]\n  for i, (dep, div, vr, vac) in enumerate(Bp['TRIG_VAC_DIVS'])],\n widths=[1.5,2.2,1.0,1.3],\n note='Table 4. Implementation window: 12 months.', bold_prefix='Phase 1 (Months 0-12): ')\nbullet('Stand up the joint Public Works fleet-maintenance shop as a shared service (3 positions absorbed, 8% fleet OT '\n       'reduction). Assumptions and Limitations', level=1)\nbullet('Salary, overtime, and process metrics derive from the FY2024 staffing/overtime workbook; 311 outcomes from the '\n       'FY2024 service-request file (500 requests, 437 closed). [S1][S2]', bold_prefix='Data basis: ')\nbullet('A1-A4 and B1-B3 parameter values (4% admin reduction, 20% fleet absorption, 8%/5% OT reductions, 10% pool '\n       'size, 40%/10% OT cuts, 60% backfill ratio, $2,000 training, $65,000 HR salaries, $2,500 per recruitment) are '\n       'analyst estimates held constant across options and documented in the workbook \"Assumptions & Sources\" tab.',\n       bold_prefix='Model assumptions: ')\nbullet('NYC is a scale benchmark, not a peer: NYC per-employee budgets cover broader service scopes; the 14.5-22.6% '\n       'ratios indicate relative compensation position only. [S3][S5]', bold_prefix='Benchmark caveat: ')\nbullet('No labor-market elasticity modeled; no capital costs; attrition timing treated as uniform over 24 months; '\n       'inflation ignored (both options evaluated in constant FY2024 dollars).', bold_prefix='Not modeled: ')\n\n# ============================ 10. RISKS ============================\ndoc.add_heading('10. prioritize Clinical Services (18.2% vacancy)'],\n ['Fire OT cap meets union resistance', 'Medium', 'Cap applies to overtime above the 10% threshold, not to base staffing; negotiate scheduling flex first'],\n ['Cross-trained pool dilutes specialty response times', 'Low-Medium', 'Pool limited to 10% of field crews; certification matrix reviewed quarterly'],\n ['Hiring yield below the 60% Year-1 assumption', 'Medium', 'Trigger re-evaluation of Phase 2 consolidation if vacancy remains >8% at Month 12'],\n ['Fleet shop consolidation stalls on facility constraints', 'Low', 'Fleet savings ($260,088) excluded from Phase 1 commitments; treat as upside']],\n widths=[2.6,1.1,3.0])\n\n# ============================ APPENDIX ============================\ndoc.add_heading('Appendix A - Source Traceability', level=1)\ntable(\n ['Tag','Source','Used for'],\n [['[S1]','Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx (Staffing_Summary; All three documents draw on the same '\n     'underlying model; figures are therefore identical across deliverables.', italic=True, size=9.5)\n\n# footer with page number\nsec = doc.sections[0]\nf = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]; f.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER\nrun = f.add_run('Decision Briefing Memo - Departmental Restructuring - Page ')\nrun.font.size = Pt(8); run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)\nfld = OxmlElement('w:fldSimple'); fld.set(qn('w:instr'), 'PAGE')\nf._p.append(fld)\n\ndoc.save('/work/output/Greenfield_Decision_Briefing_Memo.docx')\nprint('saved /work/output/Greenfield_Decision_Briefing_Memo.docx')\n"}", "type": "tool_call"}]

1: """Greenfield restructuring decision model.

3: Sources:

5:  [S2] Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv
6:  [S3] NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv (FY2025 adopted)
7:  [S4] NYC MMR indicators snapshot (dataset rbed-zzin), FY2026 citywide rows
8:  [S5] NYS Comptroller Report 2-2025, '2024 Update on NYC Staffing Trends' (May 2024)
9: """
10: import json
11: 
12: B = json.load(open('/work/scripts/baseline.json'))
13: D = ['Parks & Recreation','Sanitation','Transportation','Health Services','Fire Department']
14: st = B['depts']; ot = B['ot']; r311 = B['r311']
15: 
16: # ---- Baseline constants -------------------------------------------------
17: AUTH = {d: st[d]['auth'] for d in D}
18: FILL = {d: st[d]['fill'] for d in D}
19: VAC  = {d: st[d]['vac'] for d in D}
20: VACP = {d: st[d]['vac_pct'] for d in D}
21: SALC = {d: st[d]['salary_cost'] for d in D}          # annual base payroll of filled positions
22: OTC  = {d: ot[d]['cost'] for d in D}
23: OTR  = {d: ot[d]['oth'] for d in ot}
24: REGR = {d: ot[d]['reg'] for d in D}
25: OTPCT= {d: ot[d]['pct'] for d in D}                   # OT hours / regular hours
26: OTRATE={d: OTC[d]/OTR[d] for d in D}
27: TOT_AUTH, TOT_FILL = sum(AUTH.values()), sum(FILL.values())
28: TOT_SALC = sum(SALC.values()); TOT_OTC = sum(OTC.values())
29: CITY_OTPCT = 100*sum(OTR.values())/sum(REGR.values())
30: PER_EMP = {d: (SALC[d]+OTC[d])/FILL[d] for d in D}
31: TOT_PER_EMP = (TOT_SALC+TOT_OTC)/TOT_FILL
32: 
33: WORST_ONTIME = {'Parks & Recreation':62.4,'Sanitation':54.2,'Transportation':48.3,'Health Services':64.1,'Fire Department':59.6}
34: WORST_PROC   = {'Parks & Recreation':'Tree Removal Request','Sanitation':'Illegal Dumping Investigation',
35:                 'Transportation':'Street Resurfacing Project','Health Services':'Environmental Complaint Investigation',
36:                 'Fire Department':'Plan Review (New Construction)'}
37: AVG311 = {d: r311[d]['avg_days'] for d in D}

43:                     'Health Services':6605455698,'Fire Department':6898242822}
44: NYC_FY25_PS = {'Parks & Recreation':1421283078,'Sanitation':3352415790,'Transportation':1775724432,
45:                'Health Services':1762922085,'Fire Department':6092733423}
46: NYC_PER_EMP = {d: NYC_FY25_ADOPTED[d]/NYC_HC[d] for d in D}
47: NYC_PS_PER_EMP = {d: NYC_FY25_PS[d]/NYC_HC[d] for d in D}
48: RATIO = {d: PER_EMP[d]/NYC_PS_PER_EMP[d] for d in D}
49: NYC_VAC_OSC = {'Parks & Recreation':1.7,'Sanitation':0.0,'Transportation':10.0,'Health Services':9.3,'Fire Department':1.4}  # Jan-2024, OSC App B (Fire=uniform; DSNY=uniform)
50: 
51: # ---- PROPOSAL A ---------------------------------------------------------
52: A = {}
53: # Merged units
54: CW_AUTH, CW_FILL = AUTH['Parks & Recreation']+AUTH['Health Services'], FILL['Parks & Recreation']+FILL['Health Services']
55: PW_AUTH, PW_FILL = AUTH['Transportation']+AUTH['Sanitation'], FILL['Transportation']+FILL['Sanitation']
56: CW_WAVG = (SALC['Parks & Recreation']+SALC['Health Services'])/CW_FILL
57: PW_WAVG = (SALC['Transportation']+SALC['Sanitation'])/PW_FILL
58: # A1 admin consolidation: 4% of merged authorized positions eliminated via attrition over 24 mo
59: A1_CW_POS = round(CW_AUTH*0.04); A1_PW_POS = round(PW_AUTH*0.04)
60: A1_SAV = A1_CW_POS*CW_WAVG + A1_PW_POS*PW_WAVG
61: # A2a shared fleet maintenance: 20% of Sanitation Fleet Maintenance filled shop (17) absorbed into joint PW fleet shop
62: FLEET_FILLED, FLEET_SAL = 17, 52300
63: A2A_SAV = round(FLEET_FILLED*0.20)*FLEET_SAL      # 3 positions
64: # A2b fleet OT reduction 8% of PW OT cost
65: PW_OTC = OTC['Transportation']+OTC['Sanitation']
66: A2B_SAV = PW_OTC*0.08
67: # A3 shared field-crew deployment: 5% of PW field OT
68: A3_SAV = PW_OTC*0.05
69: # A4 Community Wellness seasonal flex: 2% of CW authorized positions
70: A4_POS = round(CW_AUTH*0.02)
71: A4_SAV = A4_POS*CW_WAVG
72: A_RECUR_SAL = A1_SAV + A2A_SAV + A4_SAV
73: A_RECUR_OT  = A2B_SAV + A3_SAV
74: A_RECUR = A_RECUR_SAL + A_RECUR_OT
75: A_POS_REMOVED = A1_CW_POS + A1_PW_POS + round(FLEET_FILLED*0.20) + A4_POS
76: A_TRANSITION = 1_200_000   # one-time, yr1 0.9M / yr2 0.3M
77: A_PHASE1, A_PHASE2 = 0.5, 1.0
78: A_NET_Y1 = A_PHASE1*A_RECUR - 0.75*A_TRANSITION
79: A_NET_Y2 = A_RECUR - 0.25*A_TRANSITION
80: # merged headcount projections (authorized)
81: A_HEADCOUNT = {'Community Wellness': CW_AUTH-A1_CW_POS-A4_POS, 'Public Works': PW_AUTH-A1_PW_POS,
82:                'Fire Department': AUTH['Fire Department']}
83: A_ONTIME_DELTA = 1.0   # indirect only

97:                  for s in staff if s['Vacancy_Rate_Pct'] > 12]
98: TRIG_VAC_DEPTS = sorted(set(x[0] for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS))
99: B_VAC_TARGET_DIVS = sum(x[3] for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS)
100: 
101: # B1 cross-training pools: 10% of field-crew filled positions in Sanitation, Transportation, Parks
102: POOL_SPEC = [('Sanitation','Refuse Collection',58),('Sanitation','Recycling Operations',26),
103:              ('Transportation','Road Maintenance',46),('Parks & Recreation','Park Maintenance',46),
104:              ('Parks & Recreation','Urban Forestry',13)]
105: B_POOL_SIZE = round(sum(p[2] for p in POOL_SPEC)*0.10)     # 19
106: B_TRAIN_COST = B_POOL_SIZE*2000      # one-time
107: B_TRAIN_MAINT = B_POOL_SIZE*500      # annual
108: # B2 shared OT budget caps (departments with annual OT>10%: Fire; Sanitation/Transportation seasonal>10%)
109: FIRE_EXCESS_H = OTR['Fire Department'] - 0.10*REGR['Fire Department']
110: FIRE_EXCESS_C = FIRE_EXCESS_H*OTRATE['Fire Department']
111: B_FIRE_CUT = 0.40*FIRE_EXCESS_C
112: B_NONFIRE_OTC = TOT_OTC - OTC['Fire Department']
113: B_NONFIRE_CUT = 0.10*B_NONFIRE_OTC
114: B_OT_SAV = B_FIRE_CUT + B_NONFIRE_CUT
115: # B3 centralized hiring (divisions vacancy>12%: Transportation x4, Health x4 => 36 vacancies)
116: B_VAC_FILL = round(0.60*sum(x[3] for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS))   # 22
117: B_HR_TEAM = 3
118: B_HR_COST = 3*65000
119: B_RECRUIT_1X = 2500*B_VAC_FILL
120: B_BACKFILL_SAL = 0
121: backfill = {}
122: for dep in TRIG_VAC_DEPTS:
123:     vacs = [x for x in TRIG_VAC_DIVS if x[0]==dep]
124:     n_dep = round(0.60*sum(x[3] for x in vacs))
125:     wavg = st[dep]['wavg_salary']
126:     backfill[dep] = dict(positions=n_dep, wavg=wavg, cost=n_dep*wavg)
127:     B_BACKFILL_SAL += n_dep*wavg
128: B_BACKFILL_OT_SAV = B_VAC_FILL*300*34.75   # 300 OT hours displaced per backfill at Transportation rate (conservative single-rate)
129: B_COST_RECUR = B_BACKFILL_SAL + B_HR_COST + B_TRAIN_MAINT
130: B_SAV = B_OT_SAV + B_BACKFILL_OT_SAV
131: B_NET_Y2 = B_SAV - B_COST_RECUR
132: B_NET_Y1 = 0.5*B_SAV - (0.5*B_BACKFILL_SAL + B_HR_COST + B_TRAIN_MAINT + B_TRAIN_COST + B_RECRUIT_1X)
133: B_ONTIME_DELTA = 8.0    # avg pts for the 7 processes <65%
134: B_FTE_TOUCHED = B_VAC_FILL + B_POOL_SIZE + B_HR_TEAM

136: # ---- HYBRID (recommended): B now + shared fleet services from A (no merger) -------------
137: H = {}
138: H_FLEET_SAV = A2A_SAV + A2B_SAV           # joint fleet shop functions as shared service
139: H_RECUR = B_SAV + H_FLEET_SAV
140: H_COST_RECUR = B_COST_RECUR
141: H_NET_Y2 = H_RECUR - H_COST_RECUR
142: H_NET_Y1 = 0.5*H_RECUR - (0.5*B_BACKFILL_SAL + B_HR_COST + B_TRAIN_MAINT + B_TRAIN_COST + B_RECRUIT_1X + 0.25*A_TRANSITION)
143: H_ONTIME_DELTA = B_ONTIME_DELTA
144: H_FTE_TOUCHED = B_FTE_TOUCHED + round(FLEET_FILLED*0.20)

146: # ---- Comparison scoring -------------------------------------------------
147: def score_a():  # savings(30) sla(30) fte(10) complexity(15) risk(15); 5=best
148:     return [5,2,3,2,2]
149: def score_b():
150:     return [2,5,4,4,4]
151: W = [0.30,0.30,0.10,0.15,0.15]
152: SA = sum(w*s for w,s in zip(W, score_a()))
153: SB = sum(w*s for w,s in zip(W, score_b()))
154: SH = 0.30*4 + 0.30*5 + 0.10*4 + 0.15*4 + 0.15*4   # hybrid: savings moderate(4: -0.61M but lower risk-adjusted), sla 5

## Goal

The user is a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield preparing a **City Council decision package** evaluating two departmental restructuring proposals for five departments (Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, Fire Department — 596 authorized / 542 filled positions). 1. **Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages)** — situation overview cross-referencing staffing vs. citizen service outcomes; NYC benchmark analysis; evaluation of each proposal on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, SLA risk, workforce feasibility; clear recommendation (one proposal or hybrid) with quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.
2. **Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx, 4 tabs)** — "Baseline Metrics" (dept scorecard: vacancy rate, OT %, avg 311 resolution days, worst on-time process %, Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio; **red conditional formatting where vacancy >12%, OT >10%, on-time <65%**), "Proposal A Model", "Proposal B Model", "Comparison Summary" (5 dimensions: annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, complexity 1–5, risk 1–5, with net recommendation score).
3. **Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides)** — operational health, trade-offs table/chart, NYC benchmark context, recommendation + next steps.

**All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across the three deliverables and traceable to source data.**

## Instructions

- **Proposal A ("Consolidate")**: merge Health Services + Parks & Recreation → "Community Wellness"; merge Transportation + Sanitation → "Public Works"; Fire standalone. Premise: shared fleet, field crews, geographic route overlap.
- **Proposal B ("Targeted Fix")**: keep 5 departments; cross-training pools; shared OT budgets for departments >10% OT-to-regular-hours; centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy >12%.

[{"content": "---

## Goal

The user is a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield preparing a **City Council decision package** evaluating two departmental restructuring proposals for five departments (Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, Fire Department — 596 authorized / 542 filled positions). Three deliverables must be produced in `/work/output/`:

1. **Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages)** — situation overview cross-referencing staffing vs. citizen service outcomes; NYC benchmark analysis; evaluation of each proposal on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, SLA risk, workforce feasibility; clear recommendation (one proposal or hybrid) with quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.
2. **Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx, 4 tabs)** — "Baseline Metrics" (dept scorecard: vacancy rate, OT %, avg 311 resolution days, worst on-time process %, Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio; **red conditional formatting where vacancy >12%, OT >10%, on-time <65%**), "Proposal A Model", "Proposal B Model", "Comparison Summary" (5 dimensions: annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, complexity 1–5, risk 1–5, with net recommendation score).
3. **Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides)** — operational health, trade-offs table/chart, NYC benchmark context, recommendation + next steps.

**All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across the three deliverables and traceable to source data.**

## Instructions

- **Proposal A ("Consolidate")**: merge Health Services + Parks & Recreation → "Community Wellness"; merge Transportation + Sanitation → "Public Works"; Fire standalone. Premise: shared fleet, field crews, geographic route overlap.
- **Proposal B ("Targeted Fix")**: keep 5 departments; cross-training pools; shared OT budgets for departments >10% OT-to-regular-hours; centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy >12%.
- Use pinned reference snapshots in `/work/task_folder/references/` (NO internet): NYC MMR indicators (dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR/DSNY/DOT/DOHMH/FDNY (SLA metrics, response-time targets) and NYS Comptroller "2024 Update on NYC Staffing Trends" (Report 2-2025).
- Local data: `Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv`, `Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx`, `NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv`.

## Discoveries

**Environment:** Python 3.12.13 with openpyxl 3.1.5, pandas 2.3.3, python-docx 1.2.0, python-pptx 1.0.2, pdfplumber 0.11.9. **NO matplotlib, NO internet** (pip failed) — use python-pptx **native charts** for visuals. The bash tool requires a `description` param on every call.

**Greenfield baseline (computed in baseline.py → baseline.json):**
- Staffing: Parks 116/110 (5.2% vac, salary $4,713,500); Sanitation 108/101 (6.5%, $4,290,100); Transportation 134/114 (14.9%, $5,545,800); Health 96/80 (16.7%, $4,835,100); Fire 142/137 (3.5%, $9,005,400). Total 596/542 = 9.06% vacancy.
- OT FY2024 (Jul23–Jun24): Parks 6.05%/$453,960; Sanitation 9.79%/$646,877 (4 months >10% = $288,021); Transportation 8.36%/$642,979 (2 months >10%); Health 7.13%/$525,390; Fire 14.57%/$2,085,312 (12/12 months >10%). Citywide 9.59%, $4,354,518 total. OT hourly rates: $32.50/$31.00/$34.75/$41.50/$48.00.
- Worst on-time processes: Parks 62.4% (Tree Removal), Sanitation 54.2% (Illegal Dumping), Transportation 48.3% (Street Resurfacing), Health 64.1% (Env Complaint), Fire 59.6% (Plan Review). **8 processes <65% citywide** (1+2+3+1+1).
- 311 (500 rows): closed 437, citywide avg 10.8 days; by dept: Fire 3.8, Sanitation 9.0, Health 12.0, Parks 12.5, Transportation 13.6; 63 unresolved avg age ~200 days; satisfaction Fire 4.23 > Health 3.72 > Sanitation 3.64 > Parks 3.55 > Transportation 3.36. Slowest categories: Crosswalk Faded 23.8d, Restaurant Inspection 18.7d, Park Maintenance 16.0d.
- All 5 departments operate in all 5 boroughs (geographic overlap confirmed).

**NYC benchmarks:**
- MMR citywide FY2026: DOT pothole % meeting 30-day close = 100 (target 98); DOHMH food-establishment SLA 90% (=target); DOHMH birth certificates 2.6d (target 3); FDNY structural fire response 4.37 min (target 4.14); FDNY EMS life-threatening 9.32 min (target 6.55); DPR memberships 27,015, attendance 15,808/mo; DSNY recycling revenue $13/ton. (In CSV, `geotype=''` = citywide.)
- OSC Report 2-2025: citywide vacancy 5.1% Jan 2024 (peak 8.4% Dec 2022; pre-pandemic 2.0%); DOT 10.0%, DOHMH 9.3%, DPR 1.7%, FDNY-uniform 1.4%, DSNY-uniform 0.0%; attrition peaked FY2022 (48,864); FDNY attrition +52% vs pre-pandemic; OT $1.8B vs $1.1B three years prior; OT share of payroll 7.0%→10.8%; FDNY Fire Extinguishing OT 28.9%→40.3% of payroll; DCAS exam turnaround 318→219 days; headcounts Jan 2024: DOT 5,117, DPR 4,384, DOHMH 5,355, FDNY 17,016, DSNY 10,137.
- NYC FY2025 adopted budgets: DOHMH $6,605.5M (PS $1,762.9M), DPR $1,914.6M (PS $1,421.3M), DSNY $5,704.3M (PS $3,352.4M), DOT $4,216.0M (PS $1,775.7M), FDNY $6,898.2M (PS $6,092.7M). NYC PS-per-employee: $324K–$358K. Greenfield/NYC-PS ratios: Parks 0.145, Sanitation 0.148, Transportation 0.156, Health 0.204, Fire 0.226 (Fire compensation closest to NYC; civilian pay lags → explains civilian turnover pattern).

**Model results (model.py → model.json):**
- **Proposal A**: CW 212 auth/190 filled (wavg $50,256); PW 242/215 (wavg $45,748). Savings: admin consolidation 4% (18 pos) $859,530 + fleet staffing 20% (3 of 17 @ $52,300) $156,900 + fleet OT 8% $103,188 + field OT 5% $64,493 + CW flex 2% (4 pos) $201,023 = **$1,385,135/yr** (25 positions removed via attrition, $1.2M one-time transition, 50% Y1 phase-in). **Net Y1 −$207,433; Net Y2 +$1,085,135**. Headcount: CW 200, PW 232, Fire 142. SLA +1.0 pt indirect; 2–5 pt temporary transition dip risk.
- **Proposal B**: Triggers — OT>10%: Fire only; vacancy>12%: 8 divisions/36 vacancies (all of Transportation + all of Health). Pool = 19 cross-trained (10% of field crews; $2,000/trainee 1x + $500/yr); Fire OT cap cuts 40% of excess ($261,466); non-fire OT cut 10% ($226,921); backfill 22 positions (60% of 36; salary $1,188,156; OT displacement 22×300h×$34.75 = $229,350); HR team 3 FTE $195,000; recruiting $55,000. **Net Y2 −$674,920; Net Y1 −$532,710**. SLA +8 pts; 44 FTE touched.
- **Hybrid (recommended)**: Proposal B now + shared fleet services from A (no merger) = savings $977,825; **Net Y2 −$414,831; Net Y1 −$702,666**; SLA +8; 47 FTE touched.
- **Scores** (weights: savings 30%/SLA 30%/FTE 10%/complexity 15%/risk 15%; 5=best): A = [5,2,3,2,2] → 3.00; B = [2,5,4,4,4] → 3.70; Hybrid = [4,5,4,4,4] → 4.30. Complexity A 4/B 2/H 3; Risk A 4/B 2/H 2.
- **Recommendation**: Hybrid — implement Proposal B now (12-month), plus Phase-2 shared fleet services (from A) without full merger.

## Accomplished

- ✅ Explored all data files (xlsx 3 sheets dumped; 311 CSV analyzed; NYC budget aggregated; MMR citywide indicators extracted; 12-page OSC PDF fully text-extracted)
- ✅ Built `baseline.py` → `baseline.json` (all baseline metrics)
- ✅ Built `model.py` → `model.json` (complete proposal A/B/hybrid cost models, triggers, scores)
- ⬜ **TODO**: Generate the three deliverables into `/work/output/`:
  1. `.xlsx` — 4 required tabs + an Assumptions/Sources tab; openpyxl conditional formatting (red where vacancy >12%, OT >10%, on-time <65%); prefer real Excel formulas for traceability
  2. `.docx` memo 6–10 pages — planned structure: header → exec summary/recommendation → situation overview (staffing × service outcomes) → NYC benchmarks (MMR + OSC) → Proposal A evaluation → Proposal B evaluation → comparison + net score → hybrid recommendation → assumptions/risks → source-traceability appendix
  3. `.pptx` 8–12 slides — title, why-now, staffing scorecard, citizen outcomes, NYC benchmark, Proposal A, Proposal B, trade-offs, native pptx chart, hybrid recommendation, next steps, assumptions
- ⬜ **TODO**: Cross-verify quantitative consistency across all three deliverables (pull all numbers from model.json/baseline.json; source tags [S1]–[S5] defined in model.py)

## Relevant files / directories

- `/work/task_folder/TASK_INSTRUCTIONS.txt` — full task spec (mirrors user prompt)
- `/work/task_folder/Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv` — 500 311 records (DPR/DSNY/DOT/DHS/FDNY codes; DHS = Health Services)
- `/work/task_folder/Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx` — sheets: Staffing_Summary (19 divisions), Monthly_Overtime (12 months × 5 depts), Process_Metrics (25 processes)
- `/work/task_folder/NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv` — NYC agency budgets FY2023–2025
- `/work/task_folder/references/NYC_MMR_Selected_Agencies.csv` — MMR indicators (1,000 rows)
- `/work/task_folder/references/NYC_Staffing_Trends_2024.pdf` — NYS Comptroller Report 2-2025 (12 pages, extracted)
- `/work/scripts/baseline.py`, `/work/scripts/baseline.json` — baseline computation + data
- `/work/scripts/model.py`, `/work/scripts/model.json` — proposal models + scores (single source of truth)
- `/work/scripts/more311.py`, `/work/scripts/nycbudget.py` — exploratory analyses
- `/work/output/` — **target directory for the three deliverables (currently empty)**

[{"content": "---

## Goal

The user is a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield preparing a **City Council decision package** evaluating two departmental restructuring proposals for five departments (Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, Fire Department — 596 authorized / 542 filled positions). Three deliverables must be produced in `/work/output/`:

1. **Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages)** — situation overview cross-referencing staffing vs. citizen service outcomes; NYC benchmark analysis; evaluation of each proposal on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, SLA risk, workforce feasibility; clear recommendation (one proposal or hybrid) with quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.
2. **Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx, 4 tabs)** — "Baseline Metrics" (dept scorecard: vacancy rate, OT %, avg 311 resolution days, worst on-time process %, Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio; **red conditional formatting where vacancy >12%, OT >10%, on-time <65%**), "Proposal A Model", "Proposal B Model", "Comparison Summary" (5 dimensions: annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, complexity 1–5, risk 1–5, with net recommendation score).
3. **Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides)** — operational health, trade-offs table/chart, NYC benchmark context, recommendation + next steps.

**All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across the three deliverables and traceable to source data.**

## Instructions

- **Proposal A ("Consolidate")**: merge Health Services + Parks & Recreation → "Community Wellness"; merge Transportation + Sanitation → "Public Works"; Fire standalone. Premise: shared fleet, field crews, geographic route overlap.
- **Proposal B ("Targeted Fix")**: keep 5 departments; cross-training pools; shared OT budgets for departments >10% OT-to-regular-hours; centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy >12%.
- Use pinned reference snapshots in `/work/task_folder/references/` (NO internet): NYC MMR indicators (dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR/DSNY/DOT/DOHMH/FDNY (SLA metrics, response-time targets) and NYS Comptroller "2024 Update on NYC Staffing Trends" (Report 2-2025).
- Local data: `Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv`, `Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx`, `NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv`.

## Discoveries

**Environment:** Python 3.12.13 with openpyxl 3.1.5, pandas 2.3.3, python-docx 1.2.0, python-pptx 1.0.2, pdfplumber 0.11.9. **NO matplotlib, NO internet** (pip failed) — use python-pptx **native charts** for visuals. The bash tool requires a `description` param on every call.

**Greenfield baseline (computed in baseline.py → baseline.json):**
- Staffing: Parks 116/110 (5.2% vac, salary $4,713,500); Sanitation 108/101 (6.5%, $4,290,100); Transportation 134/114 (14.9%, $5,545,800); Health 96/80 (16.7%, $4,835,100); Fire 142/137 (3.5%, $9,005,400). Total 596/542 = 9.06% vacancy.
- OT FY2024 (Jul23–Jun24): Parks 6.05%/$453,960; Sanitation 9.79%/$646,877 (4 months >10% = $288,021); Transportation 8.36%/$642,979 (2 months >10%); Health 7.13%/$525,390; Fire 14.57%/$2,085,312 (12/12 months >10%). Citywide 9.59%, $4,354,518 total. OT hourly rates: $32.50/$31.00/$34.75/$41.50/$48.00.
- Worst on-time processes: Parks 62.4% (Tree Removal), Sanitation 54.2% (Illegal Dumping), Transportation 48.3% (Street Resurfacing), Health 64.1% (Env Complaint), Fire 59.6% (Plan Review). **8 processes <65% citywide** (1+2+3+1+1).
- 311 (500 rows): closed 437, citywide avg 10.8 days; by dept: Fire 3.8, Sanitation 9.0, Health 12.0, Parks 12.5, Transportation 13.6; 63 unresolved avg age ~200 days; satisfaction Fire 4.23 > Health 3.72 > Sanitation 3.64 > Parks 3.55 > Transportation 3.36. Slowest categories: Crosswalk Faded 23.8d, Restaurant Inspection 18.7d, Park Maintenance 16.0d.
- All 5 departments operate in all 5 boroughs (geographic overlap confirmed).

**NYC benchmarks:**
- MMR citywide FY2026: DOT pothole % meeting 30-day close = 100 (target 98); DOHMH food-establishment SLA 90% (=target); DOHMH birth certificates 2.6d (target 3); FDNY structural fire response 4.37 min (target 4.14); FDNY EMS life-threatening 9.32 min (target 6.55); DPR memberships 27,015, attendance 15,808/mo; DSNY recycling revenue $13/ton. (In CSV, `geotype=''` = citywide.)
- OSC Report 2-2025: citywide vacancy 5.1% Jan 2024 (peak 8.4% Dec 2022; pre-pandemic 2.0%); DOT 10.0%, DOHMH 9.3%, DPR 1.7%, FDNY-uniform 1.4%, DSNY-uniform 0.0%; attrition peaked FY2022 (48,864); FDNY attrition +52% vs pre-pandemic; OT $1.8B vs $1.1B three years prior; OT share of payroll 7.0%→10.8%; FDNY Fire Extinguishing OT 28.9%→40.3% of payroll; DCAS exam turnaround 318→219 days; headcounts Jan 2024: DOT 5,117, DPR 4,384, DOHMH 5,355, FDNY 17,016, DSNY 10,137.
- NYC FY2025 adopted budgets: DOHMH $6,605.5M (PS $1,762.9M), DPR $1,914.6M (PS $1,421.3M), DSNY $5,704.3M (PS $3,352.4M), DOT $4,216.0M (PS $1,775.7M), FDNY $6,898.2M (PS $6,092.7M). NYC PS-per-employee: $324K–$358K. Greenfield/NYC-PS ratios: Parks 0.145, Sanitation 0.148, Transportation 0.156, Health 0.204, Fire 0.226 (Fire compensation closest to NYC; civilian pay lags → explains civilian turnover pattern).

**Model results (model.py → model.json):**
- **Proposal A**: CW 212 auth/190 filled (wavg $50,256); PW 242/215 (wavg $45,748). Savings: admin consolidation 4% (18 pos) $859,530 + fleet staffing 20% (3 of 17 @ $52,300) $156,900 + fleet OT 8% $103,188 + field OT 5% $64,493 + CW flex 2% (4 pos) $201,023 = **$1,385,135/yr** (25 positions removed via attrition, $1.2M one-time transition, 50% Y1 phase-in). **Net Y1 −$207,433; Net Y2 +$1,085,135**. Headcount: CW 200, PW 232, Fire 142. SLA +1.0 pt indirect; 2–5 pt temporary transition dip risk.
- **Proposal B**: Triggers — OT>10%: Fire only; vacancy>12%: 8 divisions/36 vacancies (all of Transportation + all of Health). Pool = 19 cross-trained (10% of field crews; $2,000/trainee 1x + $500/yr); Fire OT cap cuts 40% of excess ($261,466); non-fire OT cut 10% ($226,921); backfill 22 positions (60% of 36; salary $1,188,156; OT displacement 22×300h×$34.75 = $229,350); HR team 3 FTE $195,000; recruiting $55,000. **Net Y2 −$674,920; Net Y1 −$532,710**. SLA +8 pts; 44 FTE touched.
- **Hybrid (recommended)**: Proposal B now + shared fleet services from A (no merger) = savings $977,825; **Net Y2 −$414,831; Net Y1 −$702,666**; SLA +8; 47 FTE touched.
- **Scores** (weights: savings 30%/SLA 30%/FTE 10%/complexity 15%/risk 15%; 5=best): A = [5,2,3,2,2] → 3.00; B = [2,5,4,4,4] → 3.70; Hybrid = [4,5,4,4,4] → 4.30. Complexity A 4/B 2/H 3; Risk A 4/B 2/H 2.

[{"content": "---

## Goal

The user is a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield preparing a **City Council decision package** evaluating two departmental restructuring proposals for five departments (Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, Fire Department — 596 authorized / 542 filled positions). Three deliverables must be produced in `/work/output/`:

1. **Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages)** — situation overview cross-referencing staffing vs. citizen service outcomes; NYC benchmark analysis; evaluation of each proposal on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, SLA risk, workforce feasibility; clear recommendation (one proposal or hybrid) with quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.
2. **Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx, 4 tabs)** — "Baseline Metrics" (dept scorecard: vacancy rate, OT %, avg 311 resolution days, worst on-time process %, Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio; **red conditional formatting where vacancy >12%, OT >10%, on-time <65%**), "Proposal A Model", "Proposal B Model", "Comparison Summary" (5 dimensions: annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, complexity 1–5, risk 1–5, with net recommendation score).
3. **Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides)** — operational health, trade-offs table/chart, NYC benchmark context, recommendation + next steps.

**All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across the three deliverables and traceable to source data.**

## Instructions

- **Proposal A ("Consolidate")**: merge Health Services + Parks & Recreation → "Community Wellness"; merge Transportation + Sanitation → "Public Works"; Fire standalone. Premise: shared fleet, field crews, geographic route overlap.
- **Proposal B ("Targeted Fix")**: keep 5 departments; cross-training pools; shared OT budgets for departments >10% OT-to-regular-hours; centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy >12%.
- Use pinned reference snapshots in `/work/task_folder/references/` (NO internet): NYC MMR indicators (dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR/DSNY/DOT/DOHMH/FDNY (SLA metrics, response-time targets) and NYS Comptroller "2024 Update on NYC Staffing Trends" (Report 2-2025).
- Local data: `Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv`, `Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx`, `NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv`.

## Discoveries

**Environment:** Python 3.12.13 with openpyxl 3.1.5, pandas 2.3.3, python-docx 1.2.0, python-pptx 1.0.2, pdfplumber 0.11.9. **NO matplotlib, NO internet** (pip failed) — use python-pptx **native charts** for visuals. The bash tool requires a `description` param on every call.

**Greenfield baseline (computed in baseline.py → baseline.json):**
- Staffing: Parks 116/110 (5.2% vac, salary $4,713,500); Sanitation 108/101 (6.5%, $4,290,100); Transportation 134/114 (14.9%, $5,545,800); Health 96/80 (16.7%, $4,835,100); Fire 142/137 (3.5%, $9,005,400). Total 596/542 = 9.06% vacancy.
- OT FY2024 (Jul23–Jun24): Parks 6.05%/$453,960; Sanitation 9.79%/$646,877 (4 months >10% = $288,021); Transportation 8.36%/$642,979 (2 months >10%); Health 7.13%/$525,390; Fire 14.57%/$2,085,312 (12/12 months >10%). Citywide 9.59%, $4,354,518 total. OT hourly rates: $32.50/$31.00/$34.75/$41.50/$48.00.
- Worst on-time processes: Parks 62.4% (Tree Removal), Sanitation 54.2% (Illegal Dumping), Transportation 48.3% (Street Resurfacing), Health 64.1% (Env Complaint), Fire 59.6% (Plan Review). **8 processes <65% citywide** (1+2+3+1+1).
- 311 (500 rows): closed 437, citywide avg 10.8 days; by dept: Fire 3.8, Sanitation 9.0, Health 12.0, Parks 12.5, Transportation 13.6; 63 unresolved avg age ~200 days; satisfaction Fire 4.23 > Health 3.72 > Sanitation 3.64 > Parks 3.55 > Transportation 3.36. Slowest categories: Crosswalk Faded 23.8d, Restaurant Inspection 18.7d, Park Maintenance 16.0d.
- All 5 departments operate in all 5 boroughs (geographic overlap confirmed).

**NYC benchmarks:**
- MMR citywide FY2026: DOT pothole % meeting 30-day close = 100 (target 98); DOHMH food-establishment SLA 90% (=target); DOHMH birth certificates 2.6d (target 3); FDNY structural fire response 4.37 min (target 4.14); FDNY EMS life-threatening 9.32 min (target 6.55); DPR memberships 27,015, attendance 15,808/mo; DSNY recycling revenue $13/ton. (In CSV, `geotype=''` = citywide.)
- OSC Report 2-2025: citywide vacancy 5.1% Jan 2024 (peak 8.4% Dec 2022; pre-pandemic 2.0%); DOT 10.0%, DOHMH 9.3%, DPR 1.7%, FDNY-uniform 1.4%, DSNY-uniform 0.0%; attrition peaked FY2022 (48,864); FDNY attrition +52% vs pre-pandemic; OT $1.8B vs $1.1B three years prior; OT share of payroll 7.0%→10.8%; FDNY Fire Extinguishing OT 28.9%→40.3% of payroll; DCAS exam turnaround 318→219 days; headcounts Jan 2024: DOT 5,117, DPR 4,384, DOHMH 5,355, FDNY 17,016, DSNY 10,137.
- NYC FY2025 adopted budgets: DOHMH $6,605.5M (PS $1,762.9M), DPR $1,914.6M (PS $1,421.3M), DSNY $5,704.3M (PS $3,352.4M), DOT $4,216.0M (PS $1,775.7M), FDNY $6,898.2M (PS $6,092.7M). NYC PS-per-employee: $324K–$358K. Greenfield/NYC-PS ratios: Parks 0.145, Sanitation 0.148, Transportation 0.156, Health 0.204, Fire 0.226 (Fire compensation closest to NYC; civilian pay lags → explains civilian turnover pattern).

**Model results (model.py → model.json):**
- **Proposal A**: CW 212 auth/190 filled (wavg $50,256); PW 242/215 (wavg $45,748). Savings: admin consolidation 4% (18 pos) $859,530 + fleet staffing 20% (3 of 17 @ $52,300) $156,900 + fleet OT 8% $103,188 + field OT 5% $64,493 + CW flex 2% (4 pos) $201,023 = **$1,385,135/yr** (25 positions removed via attrition, $1.2M one-time transition, 50% Y1 phase-in). **Net Y1 −$207,433; Net Y2 +$1,085,135**. Headcount: CW 200, PW 232, Fire 142. SLA +1.0 pt indirect; 2–5 pt temporary transition dip risk.
- **Proposal B**: Triggers — OT>10%: Fire only; vacancy>12%: 8 divisions/36 vacancies (all of Transportation + all of Health). Pool = 19 cross-trained (10% of field crews; $2,000/trainee 1x + $500/yr); Fire OT cap cuts 40% of excess ($261,466); non-fire OT cut 10% ($226,921); backfill 22 positions (60% of 36; salary $1,188,156; OT displacement 22×300h×$34.75 = $229,350); HR team 3 FTE $195,000; recruiting $55,000. **Net Y2 −$674,920; Net Y1 −$532,710**. SLA +8 pts; 44 FTE touched.
- **Hybrid (recommended)**: Proposal B now + shared fleet services from A (no merger) = savings $977,825; **Net Y2 −$414,831; Net Y1 −$702,666**; SLA +8; 47 FTE touched.
- **Scores** (weights: savings 30%/SLA 30%/FTE 10%/complexity 15%/risk 15%; 5=best): A = [5,2,3,2,2] → 3.00; B = [2,5,4,4,4] → 3.70; Hybrid = [4,5,4,4,4] → 4.30. Complexity A 4/B 2/H 3; Risk A 4/B 2/H 2.
- **Recommendation**: Hybrid — implement Proposal B now (12-month), plus Phase-2 shared fleet services (from A) without full merger.

## Accomplished

- ✅ Explored all data files (xlsx 3 sheets dumped; 311 CSV analyzed; NYC budget aggregated; MMR citywide indicators extracted; 12-page OSC PDF fully text-extracted)
- ✅ Built `baseline.py` → `baseline.json` (all baseline metrics)
- ✅ Built `model.py` → `model.json` (complete proposal A/B/hybrid cost models, triggers, scores)

  1. `.xlsx` — 4 required tabs + an Assumptions/Sources tab; openpyxl conditional formatting (red where vacancy >12%, OT >10%, on-time <65%); prefer real Excel formulas for traceability
  2. `.docx` memo 6–10 pages — planned structure: header → exec summary/recommendation → situation overview (staffing × service outcomes) → NYC benchmarks (MMR + OSC) → Proposal A evaluation → Proposal B evaluation → comparison + net score → hybrid recommendation → assumptions/risks → source-traceability appendix
  3. `.pptx` 8–12 slides — title, why-now, staffing scorecard, citizen outcomes, NYC benchmark, Proposal A, Proposal B, trade-offs, native pptx chart, hybrid recommendation, next steps, assumptions
- ⬜ **TODO**: Cross-verify quantitative consistency across all three deliverables (pull all numbers from model.json/baseline.json; source tags [S1]–[S5] defined in model.py)

## Relevant files / directories

- `/work/task_folder/TASK_INSTRUCTIONS.txt` — full task spec (mirrors user prompt)
- `/work/task_folder/Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv` — 500 311 records (DPR/DSNY/DOT/DHS/FDNY codes; DHS = Health Services)

- `/work/scripts/baseline.py`, `/work/scripts/baseline.json` — baseline computation + data
- `/work/scripts/model.py`, `/work/scripts/model.json` — proposal models + scores (single source of truth)
